events.title: Twin Earthquake Doublet Strikes Venezuela's Central Coast
events.detail: A Mw 7.2 foreshock strikes at 18:04 local time (22:04 UTC) 20km east of San Felipe, Yaracuy state, followed 33–39 seconds later by a Mw 7.5 mainshock 20km west of Catia La Mar, La Guaira. Both events rupture at 10km depth via right-lateral strike-slip faulting along the Boconó–San Sebastián–El Pilar fault system; USGS rates the sequence PAGER RED. It is the strongest earthquake to hit Venezuela since the 1900 M7.7 San Narciso quake. GLIDE ID: EQ-2026-000093-VEN.

events.title: Tsunami Advisory Issued for Puerto Rico, Dominican Republic, US Virgin Islands
events.detail: A regional tsunami advisory is issued and later rescinded. Small waves are recorded: 4cm at Isla de Mona and Yabucoa, Puerto Rico, and 2cm at Fort-de-France, Martinique. In Trinidad, coastal uplift of up to 20 feet (6.1m) is observed at Galfa Point on the southwestern peninsula.

events.title: Government Declares State of Emergency, La Guaira a Disaster Zone
events.detail: Acting President Delcy Rodríguez declares La Guaira a 'disaster zone' and orders a nationwide state of emergency. Gas supply is shut off to prevent explosions, Caracas Metro service is suspended indefinitely, and schools nationwide are ordered closed.

events.title: Catia La Mar Children's Hospital Collapses
events.detail: A children's hospital in Catia La Mar, near the La Guaira epicenter, collapses in the mainshock, killing 16 children and injuring 35 — among the single deadliest structural failures of the disaster.

events.title: Quakes Deal Blow to Already-Battered Economy
events.detail: CNN Business analysis warns the earthquakes are a 'gut punch' to a Venezuelan economy already weakened by over a decade of sanctions, hyperinflation and mismanagement, with GDP growth projections for 2026 set to be revised sharply downward from earlier ~8% forecasts.

events.title: Death Toll Passes 920 as World Mobilizes Rescue Effort
events.detail: Confirmed deaths climb past 920 within 48 hours as international search-and-rescue teams begin arriving. Rescue convoys from Mexico, El Salvador and the Dominican Republic reach Venezuela.

events.title: US, Brazil and Others Pledge Earthquake Aid
events.detail: The US pledges a 'whole-of-government response' including $150 million in aid plus warships, transport planes and helicopters. Brazil dispatches a field hospital, 36 firefighters and 8 risk-assessment/telecoms specialists. Puerto Rican singer Bad Bunny organizes a private humanitarian aid shipment (arriving 3 July) alongside diaspora-driven relief from Colombia and Spain.

events.title: Aftershock Collapses Key La Guaira Bridge
events.detail: A significant aftershock (~M5.0) collapses the bridge connecting Caraballeda to the rest of La Guaira state, further isolating quake-hit coastal communities and complicating aid delivery.

events.title: UN Reports Death Toll Passes 1,700; Thousands Still Missing
events.detail: The death toll passes 1,700 as the UN continues scaling up its response. Reports emerge of government forces restricting or impeding international rescue teams from entering some of the hardest-hit areas; UN Under-Secretary-General Tom Fletcher cites over 50,000 people missing.

events.title: PROVEA Flags Inconsistent Government Casualty Updates
events.detail: Venezuelan human rights group PROVEA highlights inconsistencies in early official casualty reporting: the death count rose by only 20 between 27 and 28 June while the separately reported injured figure fell from 3,238 to 3,150 in the same window — raising transparency concerns later echoed by international outlets including the New York Times.

events.title: Government Launches 'Traffic Light' Building Safety Assessment
events.detail: An inspection committee combining public institutions, FUNVISIS (Venezuelan Seismological Research Foundation), the Central University of Venezuela (UCV) and other engineering bodies launches a red/yellow/green 'traffic light' system to classify structural damage and determine which buildings are safe for reoccupation.

events.title: 6,400+ Rescued; 11 International Field Hospitals Operating
events.detail: More than 6,400 people have been rescued from rubble to date. Eleven international field hospitals are now established, staffed by healthcare personnel from 33 countries.

events.title: Death Toll Reaches 2,595
events.detail: Government figures announced at an international press conference put the confirmed death toll at 2,595, more than a week after the earthquakes.

events.title: Rodríguez Accuses Foreign Media of 'Manufacturing Chaos'
events.detail: At a press conference with international correspondents at La Carlota Airport in Caracas, Acting President Delcy Rodríguez says targeted media campaigns were launched to 'manufacture chaos' and hinder search-and-rescue efforts. Interior Minister Diosdado Cabello, flanking her, urges residents to 'trust their government.'

events.title: Exiled Opposition Leader Machado Seeks Return Amid Quake Fallout
events.detail: María Corina Machado, the exiled opposition leader and 2025 Nobel Peace Prize laureate who fled Venezuela in December, says she wants to return home to help the country's 'transition process, especially after the tragedy.' Her movement launches a crowdsourced missing-persons database and mobilizes diaspora-driven aid collection.

events.title: Volunteer Registrations Reach 27,000
events.detail: Civilian volunteer registrations for the earthquake response reach 27,000, supplementing more than 14,000 deployed military personnel and thousands of foreign specialists.

events.title: Independent Tracker Lists 18,100 Missing
events.detail: The crowdsourced site 'Venezuela Te Busca' ('Venezuela Looks for You') lists 18,100 people as missing — one of several competing unofficial tallies (alongside 'Venezuela Reporta' and 'Desaparecidos Terremoto Venezuela') that would keep climbing through the summer in the absence of an official government count.

events.title: UN Appeals for Additional $296M as Response Scales Up
events.detail: UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs Tom Fletcher, briefing from Caracas, says the wider UN response needs an additional $296 million on top of the $632 million already appealed for 2026 — a $927–931 million total requirement leaving a roughly $627 million gap — to reach 1.3 million affected people over six months.

events.title: Analysis: Rodríguez Faces Her 'Worst Crisis Yet'
events.detail: CNN analysis examines whether the earthquake response strengthens or undermines Acting President Delcy Rodríguez's hold on power, describing the disaster as the most severe political test of her tenure.

events.title: NGOs Warn of Trafficking Risk to Displaced Children
events.detail: Plan International and Save the Children warn that an estimated 680,000 children across the hardest-hit areas face heightened risk of trafficking, exploitation and violence amid mass displacement and family separation. Both note no confirmed trafficking cases have yet been documented in La Guaira or northern Caracas, framing the warning as preventive.

events.title: International Rescue Teams Begin Ending Operations
events.detail: Search-and-rescue teams from Spain, the Netherlands, Colombia and the US begin winding down operations, citing diminishing chances of finding survivors more than two weeks after the earthquakes. The response formally shifts from rescue toward body recovery.

events.title: Combined Response Personnel Reach ~62,000
events.detail: Response personnel deployed nationwide reach roughly 62,300 — approximately 31,800 government responders (Civil Protection, firefighters, police, military) and 30,500 civilian volunteers — coordinating rescue, medical and shelter operations.

events.title: NPR: Earthquake Recovery Pushes Democratic Transition to the Sidelines
events.detail: NPR analysis reports that earthquake recovery has pushed Venezuela's long-stalled democratic transition further to the margins, as the government prioritizes emergency management over political negotiations amid Delcy Rodríguez's contested acting-president mandate.

events.title: Two Survivors Found Alive Nearly a Month After Quakes
events.detail: Two people are pulled alive from earthquake rubble nearly a month after the 24 June quakes, a rare and widely covered survival story amid an otherwise grim recovery phase.

events.title: Analysis: What's Next for Venezuela's Recovery Path
events.detail: Al Jazeera analysis outlines the scale of Venezuela's reconstruction challenge: tens of billions of dollars in estimated rebuilding costs, a humanitarian response plan far short of its funding target, and a housing and construction sector already weakened by years of economic crisis and sanctions.

events.title: Report: International Attention Fades as Needs Spiral
events.detail: The New Humanitarian reports that international media and donor attention is fading even as humanitarian needs continue to grow, warning of a widening gap between the scale of the crisis and resources committed to addressing it.

events.title: Government Establishes Post-Earthquake Housing Commission
events.detail: The government sets up a dedicated post-earthquake housing commission working with the Ministry of Habitat and Housing and local administrations across La Guaira, Aragua, Miranda, Carabobo and Falcón states, pledging to rehouse displaced families by the end of the year.

events.title: Death Toll Passes 6,000
events.detail: The confirmed death toll passes 6,000 more than five weeks after the earthquakes. Separately, La Guaira's state governor states 1,579 people remain missing in the state — one of several conflicting missing-persons figures circulating alongside independent trackers citing tens of thousands unaccounted for nationwide.

events.title: OCHA Situation Report #32 Published
events.detail: OCHA issues Situation Report #32, detailing the ongoing multisectoral response reaching hundreds of thousands of affected people across shelter, health, food security, WASH and protection sectors nationwide.

events.title: OCHA SitRep #33: 73,356 Given Hospital Care, 53,314 Homes Evaluated
events.detail: OCHA Situation Report #33 records 73,356 people who have received hospital or medical care since the earthquakes, 53,314 homes evaluated for structural safety (9,567 rated high-risk), and more than 304,000 people reached with humanitarian assistance and essential services through the coordinated multi-sector response.

events.title: Death Toll Rises to 6,301 per ReliefWeb SitRep #23
events.detail: ReliefWeb's Earthquake Response Situation Report #23 (covering 14–17 August) puts the confirmed death toll at 6,301 and the injured/hospitalized figure at 73,356, as the response continues scaling toward the UN's target of reaching 1.3 million affected people over six months.

events.title: Nationwide Home-Repair Program Passes 13,000 Homes
events.detail: The government's nationwide 'Venezuela Rises' home-repair program reports more than 13,000 earthquake-damaged homes under repair, targeting 66,000 beneficiaries. The first 60 rehabilitated apartments are delivered at the Ana Victoria housing complex in Vargas municipality, La Guaira state, and controlled demolitions begin on the most severely damaged structures.
